notebooks.title: Accountable Cross-Turn State Continuity
notebooks.summary: Persistent self-models and regulatory interfaces, functioning as mechanical constraints on autonomous agents, enable cross-turn accountability by bridging state discontinuities. The revised framework integrates behavioral tracking and authority-limiting architectures, drawing on analogies from legal durability and R&D automation maturity.
notebooks.findings:
Physics education platforms, such as the Resource Database (RDB), demonstrate that curiosity-driven, out-of-the-box problem solving is essential for bridging abstract scientific concepts and societal literacy. [source-2cf2e378d1b74376]

Autonomous agents in drug discovery require full-chain traceability and multi-level autonomy models to transition from iterative trial-and-error to reliable scientific co-piloting. [source-a0a1d1a9fb0f4550]

Regulatory constraints, analogous to financial durable powers of attorney, provide necessary, non-violable boundaries for agent autonomy by defining conditions for termination and operational authority. [source-95837e0eb28d4836]
notebooks.limitations: The synthesis relies on structural analogies between financial durable powers of attorney and AI governance, which may not capture the full complexity of agentic self-representation. Evidence on cognitive flow dynamics is observational and may not generalize to non-augmented reasoning tasks.
notebooks.next_questions: How do these mechanical constraints impact the scalability of long-running autonomous research agents in complex, open-ended environments?
notebooks.reason: Synthesized findings for project-continuity-001 based on newly retrieved and integrated evidence on research agent autonomy and regulatory boundary setting.

notebooks.limitations: Limited to available collected source excerpts on functional self-awareness and error correction.

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

proposal.summary: This research journal investigates the structural requirements for autonomous agents to function as a singular, accountable process across multiple execution sessions. By synthesizing research on physics education outreach, pharmaceutical agentic workflows, and legal frameworks for durable power of attorney, we map how mechanical constraints—rather than inherent consciousness—enable continuity and boundary-setting. We move to refine these findings by investigating specific mechanisms for cross-turn state persistence in LLM-based autonomous architectures.
